```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = NA)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
```

This tutorial introduces to data augmentation with the package `housepi`.
We explain the process of associating augmented variable to individuals to then proceed with standard model generation and inference.

# Augment Onset Times

For a more realistic example, we use the template model "ex-augm-onset-single-intro", where surveys are conditioned on single introduction and follow the times of onset.
For simplicity the model assumes no asymptomatic cases.

```{r}
hmc <- housepi::HouseholdModelClass$new("eg-augm-onset-single-intro")
```

This time we load the parameter definitions directly from the model template.

```{r}
# use example parameters associated to the templated model
hmc$load_param_template()

# export the data.frame with formatted parameter definitions
param_defs <- hmc$param_defs
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(param_defs)
```

## Simulate an Outbreak

We propose the following definitions for the augmented variable

```{r}
# associate defininitions from a list
hmc$load_augm_list(
  # add augmented variable definition 'onset_date'
  onset_date = list(
    init_rand = TRUE,
    model = "lnorm", args = list(meanlog = 4, sdlog = 0.5),
    max = 365
  ),
  # add augmented variable definition 'incub_period'
  incub_period = list(
    init_rand = TRUE,
    # assign arguments of incubation period from parameter definitions
    model = "gamma", args = list(shape = "inc_shape@P",
                                 scale = "inc_scale@P"),
    max = 14
  )
)

# append incubation period distribution parameters as constants
hmc$load_param_list(inc_shape = 2, inc_scale = 1.1)
```

We run a simulation with the method `simulate`.

```{r}
# override status of the dataset according to simulation
dataset <- housepi::survey
hmc$simulate(dataset = dataset, seed = 3731)

# show a summary of the current dataset # FIXME
#hmc$summarise_data()
```

In addition to the final status, the simulation associates the values of the augmented variables: the incubation period and the onset time.
Note that this simulation, as for all other templated models, do not simulate a sampling process.

```{r}
# remove incubation period from simulated dataset
dataset <- subset(hmc$dataset, select = -c(incub_period))

# change all onsets after 9 PM to next day
is_infec <- dataset$status == 1
dataset[is_infec, "onset_date"] <- sapply(
  dataset[is_infec, "onset_date"],
  function(x) if ((x %% 1) > 0.875) ceiling(x) else floor(x)
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(head(dataset))
```

## Validate the Simulation

We can check that inference returns the parameters used for the simulation.

```{r}
# load definitions from list and drop previous definitions 
hmc$load_augm_list(
  # add 'onset_date' definition
  onset_date = list(
    value = "onset_date@D",
    rule = "norm", rule_scale = 0.25,
    rule_from = "onset_date@D"
  ),
  # add 'incub_period' definition
  incub_period = list(
    init_rand = TRUE,
    model = "gamma", args = list(shape = "inc_shape@P",
                                 scale = "inc_scale@P"),
    rule = "gibbs", max = 14
  ),
  append = FALSE # we drop previous definitions
)

# perform the inference
# note: NA onset dates of healthy individuals will raise a warning
hmc$infer(dataset = dataset, n_steps = 10000, n_burnin = 1000, thin = 10,
          n_chains = 3, n_adapt = 2000, seed = 3413, progress = TRUE)
```

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=4, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
# plot the traces of all chains 
lattice::xyplot(hmc$traces)
```

```{r}
# collect the results
results <- hmc$traces_results

# compare results to parameter values used for inference
imask <- param_defs$constant == FALSE
inames <- param_defs[imask, ]$name

check <- cbind(expec = param_defs[imask, ]$value, results)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(check, digits = 3)

# cross-machine checking
# Mean	SD	Q2.5	Q97.5	Simul
# alpha	0.000	0.000	0.000	0.000	0.00
# beta	0.051	0.006	0.039	0.063	0.07
# gamma	1.191	0.326	0.524	1.829	0.85
# inf_vacc	0.861	0.310	0.364	1.577	0.50
# sus_vacc	0.383	0.182	0.101	0.809	0.25
```

### Model Comparison

We can estimate the model evidence (or marginal loglikelihood) with the method of the power posteriors:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# return the estimate of the model evidence
hmc$evidence(n_rungs = 30)
```
